# A gate edit locks the conductor out

**Symptom.** Right after a worker edits `claude/hooks/conductor-gate.sh`, every conductor tool call is denied, including `harness` and `cat .harness/...`, with no useful message.

**Cause.** The gate is live: `~/.claude/settings.json` points at the repo file, and it is fail-closed (decision 0005), so a script that exits non-zero denies everything. An unescaped `$(` inside a double-quoted message string was enough (commit 4d9b627 fixed it).

**Fix.** Treat the gate like `bin/`: edit through a new inode (Edit tool or tmp + mv), run `bash -n` and `bash tests/gate.test.sh` before every save, and escape `\$(` and backticks in message strings. If the conductor is already locked out, fix the file from a worker pane; the conductor needs no restart.

# Rewriting a bin/ script in place breaks the processes running it

**Symptom.** A headless analyst run ended with "gone without a result" (exit 3) at 05:04:34Z and never wrote `exit.json`, though claude itself was healthy.

**Cause.** `bin/` is symlinked into PATH, so a worker's edit hits scripts that conductor and runner processes are executing. Bash reads a script by byte offset as it goes; an in-place write (`open(p, 'w')`, `> file`, same inode) makes the running shell continue in the middle of the new text. The implementer had rewritten `bin/harness-run` that way while it sat in `wait`.

**Fix.** The bodies of `bin/harness`, `harness-run`, `harness-view` and `harness-verify` are one `{ ...; exit $?; }` group, so bash parses the whole file first. Still edit with the Edit tool or write a temp file and `mv` it (new inode); never `>` onto a `bin/*` file. A new script in `bin/` must use the same wrapper.

**lib/ files.** `bin/harness` sources `lib/harness-*.sh` eagerly at the top of the brace group, from an explicit list. bash 3.2 `source` reads the whole file into memory before running it (design experiment: a sourced file that overwrote itself mid-run kept printing its original lines; run directly it executed the injected text), so the same protection holds, but only while sourcing stays eager and lib files hold definitions only. Never source a lib file lazily (e.g. inside `ask_finish`): it could load a half-written file.

**Evidence.** ask 1792731600-29108-22965; transcript 46cb17a4 at 05:04:32Z; test "in-place rewrite" in `tests/headless.test.sh`; lib/: `tests/harness-split.test.sh` (overwrites bin/harness and every lib file mid-run), `.harness/harness-split-design.md` §4.

# Conductor shell: one allowed command per call

**Symptom.** The gate denies `herdr agent wait … | tail -5; harness status`, `harness close reviewer; echo rc=$?`, and `harness help 2>&1 | head` with "Conductor shell is limited to …", even though every part is allowed on its own.

**Cause.** Since v21 the gate accepts exactly one simple command. Any unquoted `;`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` (so `2>&1` too), `#`, backtick, `$(` or newline denies the call, and `jq`, `tail`, `head`, `echo` are not on the allowlist. (Before v21 chains were split and checked per segment and `| jq` was allowed; usage showed 44 of 754 calls chained, 0 piped.)

**Fix.** Send one allowed command per Bash call, and send independent ones in parallel. To read files, use the Read tool under `.harness/` or `docs/` instead of `cat | head`.

# Conductor shell: one allowed command per call

**Symptom.** The gate denies `herdr agent wait … | tail -5; harness status`, `harness close reviewer; echo rc=$?`, and `harness help 2>&1 | head` with "Conductor shell is limited to …", even though every part is allowed on its own.

**Cause.** Since v21 the gate accepts exactly one simple command. Any unquoted `;`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` (so `2>&1` too), `#`, backtick, `$(` or newline denies the call, and `jq`, `tail`, `head`, `echo` are not on the allowlist. (Before v21 chains were split and checked per segment and `| jq` was allowed; usage showed 44 of 754 calls chained, 0 piped.)

**Fix.** Send one allowed command per Bash call, and send independent ones in parallel. To read files, use the Read tool under `.harness/` or `docs/` instead of `cat | head`.

  local agent=$1

  [ "$agent" != implementer ] || ASK_TIMEOUT=$IMPLEMENTER_TIMEOUT

#!/bin/bash
# conductor-gate.sh — PreToolUse hook for the Fable conductor.
# Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-herdr-conductor-setup-design.md
#
# Role:   hook input agent_type -> conductor: gate; any other agent: allow
#         (only when agent_id is absent; a subagent, agent_id set, uses the env rule)
#         (herdr workers run as analyst/implementer/reviewer/solo). Keying on the
#         agent, not the env, closes the daemon-inherits-worker-env hole: a
#         conductor hosted by a daemon that exported HARNESS_ROLE=worker is still
#         gated. Without agent_type, HARNESS_ROLE=worker allows (older hosts).
#         Harness checkout: the gate acts only where .harness/asks/ exists (nearest
#                                 dir from the cwd up to the .git dir; decision 0010).
#                                 Elsewhere it allows everything, before jq or parsing,
#                                 so it never touches a repo that does not use the harness.
#                                 HERDR_ENV is ignored.
#         otherwise            -> conductor rules below
# Output: nothing (allow) or a PreToolUse deny JSON on stdout. Always exit 0.
set -u

# harness_root DIR -> prints the harness checkout root and returns 0, or returns 1.
# DIR is resolved physically (pwd -P) first, like enter_root.
# The root is the nearest dir at or above DIR with .harness/asks/, searched up to
# the dir holding .git (file or dir) inclusive; outside git only DIR counts. Same
# rule as enter_root in bin/harness-verify. This body is copied byte-for-byte into
# conductor-gate and -resume (tests/gate.test.sh checks it).
harness_root() {
  local start d hit=""
  start=$(cd "${1:-/}" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
  d=$start
  while :; do
    if [ -z "$hit" ] && [ -d "$d/.harness/asks" ]; then hit=$d; fi
    if [ -e "$d/.git" ]; then
      [ -n "$hit" ] || return 1
      printf '%s' "$hit"
      return 0
    fi
    [ "$d" = / ] && break
    d=${d%/*}
    [ -n "$d" ] || d=/
  done
  [ -d "$start/.harness/asks" ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$start"
}

INPUT=$(cat)

DIR=$PWD
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  c=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r 'if type == "object" then (.cwd // empty) else empty end' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -d "$c" ]; then DIR=$c; fi
fi
harness_root "$DIR" >/dev/null || exit 0

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # fail closed; static JSON because jq is unavailable
  printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Conductor gate requires jq. Install jq, or run a worker session."}}'
  exit 0
fi

TOOL=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty' 2>/dev/null)
if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$TOOL" ]; then
  # fail closed (decision 0005): a gate that allows what it cannot read is no gate
  echo "conductor-gate: unparseable hook input, denying" >&2
  printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Conductor gate could not parse the hook input, so the call is denied. Retry, or delegate with /analyze or /implement."}}'
  exit 0
fi

# agent_id is set only for subagents (and forked skills) inside a session. Their
# hook input carries their OWN agent_type (e.g. "tiny"), not the session's, so
# agent_type alone would wave a conductor's subagent through: the agent_id check
# catches it and falls back to the env rule.
AGENT=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.agent_type // empty' 2>/dev/null)
AGENT_ID=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.agent_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$AGENT" ] && [ -z "$AGENT_ID" ]; then
  [ "$AGENT" = conductor ] || exit 0
elif [ "${HARNESS_ROLE:-conductor}" = worker ]; then
  exit 0
fi

CWD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$CWD" ] || CWD=$PWD
CWD=${CWD%/}

# Fixed strings: never interpolate per-call data (keeps the prompt cache stable).
MSG_WRITE="Conductor cannot edit source. Delegate with the /implement skill (implementer worker). Direct writes are allowed only under docs/**/*.md and .harness/."
MSG_READ="Conductor does not read source. Delegate with the /analyze skill (analyst worker) and read its report. Direct reads are allowed only under .harness/, docs/, and *.md files."
MSG_WATCH="harness watch is for a human terminal; the conductor reads the report (harness report <worker>, or harness wait <worker> to block until the run ends)."
MSG_BASH="Conductor shell is limited to ONE command per call: harness; gh pr create|view|list|checks|comment|edit|merge (no api, no merge -d); herdr pane get|current; git status / log / diff --stat / branch (list); cat or ls (no -R) under .harness/ and docs/. No ; & | redirects, backticks or \$(. Delegate command execution with the /implement skill (implementer worker)."

# --- Bash allow/deny lists ---------------------------------------------------
# Each piece below is one alternative; they are joined with | into one regex.

# Commands the conductor may run (matched against a whole masked segment).
BASH_ALLOW='harness( .*)?'                                        # delegation CLI
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'herdr pane (get|current)( .*)?'        # herdr, read-only state ...
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'gh( .*)?'                               # GitHub CLI (see GH_ALLOW, gh_segment_ok)
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git status( (-[sb]+|--short|--branch|--porcelain(=v[12])?|--untracked-files=(no|normal|all)))*' # read-only git; no -v (prints diffs) ...
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git log( .*)?'
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git diff --stat( .*)?'                  # ... summaries only
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git branch( (-a|-r|-v|--show-current))*'  # list only
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'cat (\.harness|docs)(/[^ ]*)?'          # reports and docs
BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'ls( -[A-Za-z]+)*( (\.harness|docs)(/[^ ]*)?)?' # top level, reports, docs
BASH_ALLOW="^($BASH_ALLOW)\$"

# gh "<group> <subcommand>" pairs the conductor may run. api, run, issue, repo,
# auth, browse, pr diff|checkout|status are not here.
GH_ALLOW='pr (create|view|list|checks|comment|edit|merge)'

# git long options that are denied anywhere in a git segment.
GIT_DENY_LONG='output'                                            # writes files
GIT_DENY_LONG="$GIT_DENY_LONG|delete|move|copy"                   # mutates branches
GIT_DENY_LONG="$GIT_DENY_LONG|patch|unified|cc|binary|remerge-diff|dd|diff-merges|raw|check" # prints diff content

# Initials of git short-flag groups that are denied (e.g. -D, -Df, -U3):
#   o = --output (writes files)
#   d D m M c C = branch delete / move / copy (mutates branches)
#   p u U = patch / unified context (prints diff content)
#   G S = git log pickaxe (probes file contents)
GIT_DENY_SHORT='odDmMcCpuUGS'

GIT_DENY="--($GIT_DENY_LONG)| -[$GIT_DENY_SHORT][A-Za-z0-9]* "

deny() {
  jq -n --arg r "$1" \
    '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
  exit 0
}

field() { printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r ".tool_input.$1 // empty" 2>/dev/null; }

# rel PATH -> prints the path relative to CWD, or returns 1 when the path is
# empty, outside CWD, or contains a '..' segment.
rel() {
  local p=$1
  [ -n "$p" ] || return 1
  case "$p" in
    ..|../*|*/..|*/../*|'~'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$p" in
    "$CWD")   p="." ;;
    "$CWD"/*) p=${p#"$CWD"/} ;;
    /*)       return 1 ;;
    ./*)      p=${p#./} ;;
  esac
  printf '%s' "$p"
}

# physrel PATH -> prints the symlink-resolved path relative to the resolved CWD
# ("." for CWD itself); returns 1 when it resolves outside CWD, loops, or
# exceeds 16 symlink hops. Needs only cd -P / pwd -P / readlink (bash 3.2, BSD).
# A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing ancestor.
physrel() {
  local p=$1 root full
  root=$(physical "$CWD") || return 1
  case "$p" in /*) ;; *) p=$CWD/$p ;; esac
  full=$(physical "$p") || return 1
  case "$full" in
    "$root") printf '.' ;;
    "$root"/*) printf '%s' "${full#"$root"/}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

# physical ABS_PATH -> prints the fully resolved absolute path
physical() {
  local p=$1 hops=0 ex tail par t
  while :; do
    ex=$p; tail=""
    while [ ! -e "$ex" ] && [ ! -L "$ex" ]; do
      [ "$ex" != / ] || return 1
      tail="/${ex##*/}$tail"
      ex=${ex%/*}
      [ -n "$ex" ] || ex=/
    done
    if [ -L "$ex" ]; then
      hops=$((hops + 1))
      [ "$hops" -le 16 ] || return 1
      t=$(readlink "$ex") || return 1
      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      case "$t" in /*) p=$t$tail ;; *) p=$par/$t$tail ;; esac
      continue
    fi
    case "$tail" in */..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
    if [ -d "$ex" ]; then
      par=$(cd -P "$ex" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '%s' "$tail"; else printf '%s' "$par$tail"; fi
    else
      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '/%s%s' "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; else printf '%s/%s%s' "$par" "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; fi
    fi
    return 0
  done
}

# readable_rel / writable_rel REL -> 0 when the repo-relative path is allowed
# raw_stream_rel REL -> 0 for a headless run's raw stream (.harness/log/*.jsonl[.gz]); it
# holds source the conductor must not see (decision 0007)
raw_stream_rel() {
  local l
  l=$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')   # macOS volumes are case-insensitive
  case "$l" in .harness/log/*.jsonl|.harness/log/*.jsonl.*) return 0 ;; esac
  return 1
}
readable_rel() {
  raw_stream_rel "$1" && return 1
  case "$1" in
    .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*|*.md) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
writable_rel() {
  case "$1" in
    .harness/*) return 0 ;;
    docs/*.md)  return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# readable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may read it (lexically and after
# resolving symlinks)
readable() {
  local p
  p=$(rel "$1") || return 1
  readable_rel "$p" || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$1") || return 1
  readable_rel "$p"
}

# writable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may write it (lexically and after
# resolving symlinks)
writable() {
  local p
  p=$(rel "$1") || return 1
  writable_rel "$p" || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$1") || return 1
  writable_rel "$p"
}

# scan_command -> reads ONE command on stdin, scans it like the shell (single
# quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and prints "<masked><TAB><raw>".
# <masked> is the command with the contents of every '...' / "..." removed
# (quote chars kept); <raw> is the text as written. Exits 1 (= deny) on anything
# that would make it more than one simple command: an unquoted ; & | < > # `
# or newline, an unquoted $( $' $", ` or $( inside double quotes, an
# unterminated quote. Newlines inside quotes are kept as spaces.
# Input must not contain tabs (callers normalize them to spaces).
scan_command() {
  awk '
    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; m = ""; r = ""; nl = 0 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double
    {
      line = $0; n = length(line)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr(line, i, 1); nx = substr(line, i + 1, 1)
        if (st == 0) {
          if (c == "\\") { c = c substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++; m = m c; r = r c }
          else if (c == ";" || c == "&" || c == "|" || c == "<" || c == ">" || c == "#" || c == "`") bad = 1
          else if (c == "$" && (nx == "(" || nx == "\047" || nx == "\"")) bad = 1
          else {
            m = m c; r = r c
            if (c == "\047") st = 1
            else if (c == "\"") st = 2
          }
        } else if (st == 1) {
          r = r c
          if (c == "\047") { m = m c; st = 0 }
        } else {
          r = r c
          if (c == "\\") { r = r substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++ }
          else if (c == "\"") { m = m c; st = 0 }
          else if (c == "`" || (c == "$" && nx == "(")) bad = 1
        }
      }
      if (st == 0) nl++; else r = r " "
    }
    END { if (st != 0 || bad || nl > 1) exit 1; print m "\t" r }
  '
}


# has_expansion TEXT -> 0 when TEXT contains a character that the shell would
# expand or glob ($ { } * ? [ ] ~ \)
has_expansion() {
  case "$1" in
    *[\$\{\}\*\?\[\]~\\]*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# git_segment_ok RAW -> 0 when a git segment uses no denied option and no
# rev:path (flag checks run on the raw text with quoting removed: "-D" == -D)
git_segment_ok() {
  local norm
  norm=$(printf ' %s ' "$1" | tr -d "\"'\\\\")
  case "$norm" in *:*) return 1 ;; esac
  printf '%s' "$norm" | grep -Eq -- "$GIT_DENY" && return 1
  return 0
}

# plain_tok TOKEN -> 0 when TOKEN has no quote or backslash
plain_tok() {
  case "$1" in *[\"\'\\]*) return 1 ;; esac
  return 0
}

# bodyfile_ok VALUE -> 0 when a gh --body-file / -F value is a path that stays
# (symlinks resolved) under .harness/ or docs/. "-" (stdin) is denied.
bodyfile_ok() {
  local v=$1 p
  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != - ] || return 1
  plain_tok "$v" || return 1
  has_expansion "$v" && return 1
  p=$(rel "$v") || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$v") || return 1
  raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
  case "$p" in .harness/*|docs/*) return 0 ;; esac
  return 1
}

# gh_segment_ok MASKED RAW -> 0 only for "gh pr <sub>" with <sub> in GH_ALLOW
# (merge without -d). Global flags -R/--repo/--hostname (and --x=y) may precede
# the group. Everything up to and including the subcommand is read from the
# MASKED segment and must be plain unquoted tokens, so quoting cannot make this
# parser disagree with gh. --body-file/-F values must be plain paths under
# .harness/ or docs/. Flag checks on the rest of the segment use the raw text
# with quoting removed, so "--delete-branch" == --delete-branch.
gh_segment_ok() {
  local norm tok group sub nflag=0 mflag=0 want=0 v
  norm=$(printf '%s ' "$2" | tr -d "\"'\\\\" | tr -s ' ')
  set -f
  set -- $1
  set +f
  shift   # "gh"
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    plain_tok "$1" || return 1
    case "$1" in
      -R|--repo|--hostname) [ $# -ge 2 ] || return 1; plain_tok "$2" || return 1; shift 2 ;;
      --repo=*|--hostname=*) shift ;;
      -*) return 1 ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
  group=$1
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
  sub=$1
  shift
  plain_tok "$sub" || return 1
  printf '%s' "$group $sub" | grep -Eq "^($GH_ALLOW)\$" || return 1
  # --body-file / -F values (also --body-file=x, -Fx, clusters like -dF): read
  # from the masked tail, must be plain paths under .harness/ or docs/
  for tok in "$@"; do
    if [ "$want" -eq 1 ]; then want=0; bodyfile_ok "$tok" || return 1; continue; fi
    case "$tok" in
      --body-file|--recover) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); want=1 ;;
      --body-file=*|--recover=*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); bodyfile_ok "${tok#*=}" || return 1 ;;
      --*) ;;
      -*F*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); v=${tok#*F}
            if [ -n "$v" ]; then bodyfile_ok "$v" || return 1; else want=1; fi ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "$want" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  # quote-stripped view: a flag that only appears once quotes are removed
  # ("--body-file") must not slip past the check above, and the per-command
  # flag denials apply to it
  set -f
  set -- $norm
  set +f
  for tok in "$@"; do
    case "$tok" in
      --body-file|--body-file=*|--recover|--recover=*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
      --delete-branch|--delete-branch=*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
      --*) ;;
      -*F*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
    esac
    case "$tok" in
      --*) ;;
      -*d*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "$nflag" -le "$mflag" ] || return 1
  return 0
}

# unquoted_text_ok RAW -> 0 when the segment's shell text is plain. Outside
# quotes only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ % + , : - = and spaces are allowed, and a word
# may not start with = (zsh =cmd) or ~. That rules out braces, globs, glob
# qualifiers, expansions, backslashes, redirects and history bangs in one go.
# Single-quoted text is literal. Double-quoted text may not contain $ ` \ or !.
unquoted_text_ok() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | LC_ALL=C awk '
    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; ws = 1 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double; ws: still at word start
    { n = length($0)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr($0, i, 1)
        if (st == 1) { if (c == "\047") st = 0; else ws = 0 }
        else if (st == 2) {
          if (c == "\"") st = 0
          else {
            ws = 0
            if (c == "$" || c == "`" || c == "\\" || c == "!") bad = 1
          }
        } else if (c == " ") ws = 1
        else if (c == "\047") st = 1            # quotes alone do not end word start
        else if (c == "\"") st = 2
        else if (c == "\\") {                   # only \'"'"', \" and "\ " are literal
          nx = substr($0, i + 1, 1)
          if (nx == "\047" || nx == "\"" || nx == " ") { i++; ws = 0 } else bad = 1
        }
        else if (c ~ /[A-Za-z0-9._\/@%+,:-]/) ws = 0
        else if (c == "=" && !ws) ws = 0
        else bad = 1
      } }
    END { exit (bad || st != 0) ? 1 : 0 }'
}

# cat_ls_segment_ok MASKED -> 0 when a cat / ls segment needs no quoting,
# expansion or parent-directory access
cat_ls_segment_ok() {
  local tok p
  case "$1" in *[\"\']*|*..*) return 1 ;; esac
  has_expansion "$1" && return 1
  set -f
  set -- $1
  set +f
  case "$1" in
    ls)
      shift
      for tok in "$@"; do
        case "$tok" in
          --r*) return 1 ;;            # --recursive (and abbreviations)
          --*) ;;
          -*R*) return 1 ;;            # -R, -laR, ...
          -*) ;;
          *)  p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1   # symlink-resolved path argument
              case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    cat)
      shift
      for tok in "$@"; do        # symlink-resolved: must stay in .harness/ or docs/
        p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1
        raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
        case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
      done ;;
  esac
  return 0
}

# bash_ok COMMAND -> 0 when COMMAND is one simple command on the allowlist
bash_ok() {
  local cmd=$1 out seg raw tab
  tab=$(printf '\t')
  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
  cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | tr '\t' ' ')
  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | scan_command) || return 1
  seg=${out%%"$tab"*}
  raw=${out#*"$tab"}
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
  raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
  [ -n "$seg" ] || return 1
  # plain shell text only (character allowlist)
  unquoted_text_ok "$raw" || return 1
  # reject '..' path components (but not git ranges like main...HEAD)
  printf ' %s ' "$seg" | grep -Eq '[ /=]\.\.([ /]|$)' && return 1
  case "$seg" in
    git\ *)          git_segment_ok "$raw" || return 1
                     ;;
    gh|gh\ *)        gh_segment_ok "$seg" "$raw" || return 1 ;;
    cat\ *|ls|ls\ *) cat_ls_segment_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq "$BASH_ALLOW"
}

case "$TOOL" in
  Edit|Write)
    writable "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_WRITE" ;;
  Read)
    readable "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_READ" ;;
  Grep)
    readable "$(field path)" || deny "$MSG_READ"
    # a directory search would read the raw streams under .harness/log
    GRP=$(physrel "$(field path)") || deny "$MSG_READ"
    case "$GRP" in .harness|.harness/log) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac ;;
  Glob)
    PATTERN=$(field pattern)
    case "$PATTERN" in *..*|/*|'~'*) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac
    GPATH=$(field path)
    if [ -z "$GPATH" ]; then
      # no path: the pattern itself must stay under .harness/ or docs/
      case "$PATTERN" in docs/*|.harness/*) ;; *) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac
      GBASE=$CWD
    else
      readable "$GPATH" || deny "$MSG_READ"
      GBASE=$GPATH
      case "$GBASE" in /*) ;; *) GBASE=$CWD/$GBASE ;; esac

BASH_ALLOW="$BASH_ALLOW|"'git diff --stat( .*)?'                  # ... summaries only

GIT_DENY_LONG="$GIT_DENY_LONG|patch|unified|cc|binary|remerge-diff|dd|diff-merges|raw|check" # prints diff content

#   o = --output (writes files)
#   d D m M c C = branch delete / move / copy (mutates branches)
#   p u U = patch / unified context (prints diff content)
#   G S = git log pickaxe (probes file contents)

GIT_DENY="--($GIT_DENY_LONG)| -[$GIT_DENY_SHORT][A-Za-z0-9]* "

deny() {
  jq -n --arg r "$1" \
    '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'

field() { printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r ".tool_input.$1 // empty" 2>/dev/null; }

# rel PATH -> prints the path relative to CWD, or returns 1 when the path is
# empty, outside CWD, or contains a '..' segment.
rel() {
  local p=$1
  [ -n "$p" ] || return 1
  case "$p" in
    ..|../*|*/..|*/../*|'~'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$p" in
    "$CWD")   p="." ;;
    "$CWD"/*) p=${p#"$CWD"/} ;;
    /*)       return 1 ;;
    ./*)      p=${p#./} ;;
  esac
  printf '%s' "$p"
}

# physrel PATH -> prints the symlink-resolved path relative to the resolved CWD
# ("." for CWD itself); returns 1 when it resolves outside CWD, loops, or
# exceeds 16 symlink hops. Needs only cd -P / pwd -P / readlink (bash 3.2, BSD).
# A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing ancestor.
physrel() {
  local p=$1 root full
  root=$(physical "$CWD") || return 1
  case "$p" in /*) ;; *) p=$CWD/$p ;; esac
  full=$(physical "$p") || return 1
  case "$full" in
    "$root") printf '.' ;;
    "$root"/*) printf '%s' "${full#"$root"/}" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

# physical ABS_PATH -> prints the fully resolved absolute path
physical() {
  local p=$1 hops=0 ex tail par t
  while :; do
    ex=$p; tail=""
    while [ ! -e "$ex" ] && [ ! -L "$ex" ]; do
      [ "$ex" != / ] || return 1
      tail="/${ex##*/}$tail"
      ex=${ex%/*}
      [ -n "$ex" ] || ex=/
    done
    if [ -L "$ex" ]; then
      hops=$((hops + 1))
      [ "$hops" -le 16 ] || return 1
      t=$(readlink "$ex") || return 1
      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      case "$t" in /*) p=$t$tail ;; *) p=$par/$t$tail ;; esac
      continue
    fi
    case "$tail" in */..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
    if [ -d "$ex" ]; then
      par=$(cd -P "$ex" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '%s' "$tail"; else printf '%s' "$par$tail"; fi
    else
      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '/%s%s' "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; else printf '%s/%s%s' "$par" "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; fi
    fi
    return 0
  done
}

# raw_stream_rel REL -> 0 for a headless run's raw stream (.harness/log/*.jsonl[.gz]); it
# holds source the conductor must not see (decision 0007)

  l=$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')   # macOS volumes are case-insensitive
  case "$l" in .harness/log/*.jsonl|.harness/log/*.jsonl.*) return 0 ;; esac

  raw_stream_rel "$1" && return 1
  case "$1" in
    .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*|*.md) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}
writable_rel() {
  case "$1" in
    .harness/*) return 0 ;;
    docs/*.md)  return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# readable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may read it (lexically and after
# resolving symlinks)
readable() {
  local p
  p=$(rel "$1") || return 1
  readable_rel "$p" || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$1") || return 1
  readable_rel "$p"
}

# writable PATH -> 0 when the conductor may write it (lexically and after
# resolving symlinks)
writable() {
  local p
  p=$(rel "$1") || return 1
  writable_rel "$p" || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$1") || return 1
  writable_rel "$p"
}

# scan_command -> reads ONE command on stdin, scans it like the shell (single
# quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and prints "<masked><TAB><raw>".
# <masked> is the command with the contents of every '...' / "..." removed
# (quote chars kept); <raw> is the text as written. Exits 1 (= deny) on anything
# that would make it more than one simple command: an unquoted ; & | < > # `
# or newline, an unquoted $( $' $", ` or $( inside double quotes, an
# unterminated quote. Newlines inside quotes are kept as spaces.
# Input must not contain tabs (callers normalize them to spaces).
scan_command() {
  awk '
    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; m = ""; r = ""; nl = 0 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double
    {
      line = $0; n = length(line)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr(line, i, 1); nx = substr(line, i + 1, 1)
        if (st == 0) {
          if (c == "\\") { c = c substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++; m = m c; r = r c }
          else if (c == ";" || c == "&" || c == "|" || c == "<" || c == ">" || c == "#" || c == "`") bad = 1
          else if (c == "$" && (nx == "(" || nx == "\047" || nx == "\"")) bad = 1
          else {
            m = m c; r = r c
            if (c == "\047") st = 1
            else if (c == "\"") st = 2
          }
        } else if (st == 1) {
          r = r c
          if (c == "\047") { m = m c; st = 0 }
        } else {
          r = r c
          if (c == "\\") { r = r substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++ }
          else if (c == "\"") { m = m c; st = 0 }
          else if (c == "`" || (c == "$" && nx == "(")) bad = 1
        }
      }
      if (st == 0) nl++; else r = r " "
    }
    END { if (st != 0 || bad || nl > 1) exit 1; print m "\t" r }
  '
}


# has_expansion TEXT -> 0 when TEXT contains a character that the shell would
# expand or glob ($ { } * ? [ ] ~ \)
has_expansion() {
  case "$1" in
    *[\$\{\}\*\?\[\]~\\]*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  return 1
}

# git_segment_ok RAW -> 0 when a git segment uses no denied option and no
# rev:path (flag checks run on the raw text with quoting removed: "-D" == -D)
git_segment_ok() {

  norm=$(printf ' %s ' "$1" | tr -d "\"'\\\\")
  case "$norm" in *:*) return 1 ;; esac
  printf '%s' "$norm" | grep -Eq -- "$GIT_DENY" && return 1
  return 0
}

# plain_tok TOKEN -> 0 when TOKEN has no quote or backslash
plain_tok() {
  case "$1" in *[\"\'\\]*) return 1 ;; esac
  return 0
}

# bodyfile_ok VALUE -> 0 when a gh --body-file / -F value is a path that stays
# (symlinks resolved) under .harness/ or docs/. "-" (stdin) is denied.
bodyfile_ok() {
  local v=$1 p
  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != - ] || return 1
  plain_tok "$v" || return 1
  has_expansion "$v" && return 1
  p=$(rel "$v") || return 1
  p=$(physrel "$v") || return 1
  raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
  case "$p" in .harness/*|docs/*) return 0 ;; esac
  return 1

# (merge without -d). Global flags -R/--repo/--hostname (and --x=y) may precede
# the group. Everything up to and including the subcommand is read from the
# MASKED segment and must be plain unquoted tokens, so quoting cannot make this
# parser disagree with gh. --body-file/-F values must be plain paths under
# .harness/ or docs/. Flag checks on the rest of the segment use the raw text
# with quoting removed, so "--delete-branch" == --delete-branch.
gh_segment_ok() {
  local norm tok group sub nflag=0 mflag=0 want=0 v
  norm=$(printf '%s ' "$2" | tr -d "\"'\\\\" | tr -s ' ')
  set -f
  set -- $1
  set +f
  shift   # "gh"
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    plain_tok "$1" || return 1
    case "$1" in
      -R|--repo|--hostname) [ $# -ge 2 ] || return 1; plain_tok "$2" || return 1; shift 2 ;;
      --repo=*|--hostname=*) shift ;;
      -*) return 1 ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done

  group=$1
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
  sub=$1
  shift
  plain_tok "$sub" || return 1
  printf '%s' "$group $sub" | grep -Eq "^($GH_ALLOW)\$" || return 1

  # from the masked tail, must be plain paths under .harness/ or docs/

    if [ "$want" -eq 1 ]; then want=0; bodyfile_ok "$tok" || return 1; continue; fi
    case "$tok" in
      --body-file|--recover) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); want=1 ;;
      --body-file=*|--recover=*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); bodyfile_ok "${tok#*=}" || return 1 ;;
      --*) ;;
      -*F*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); v=${tok#*F}
            if [ -n "$v" ]; then bodyfile_ok "$v" || return 1; else want=1; fi ;;
    esac

  # ("--body-file") must not slip past the check above, and the per-command
  # flag denials apply to it
  set -f
  set -- $norm
  set +f

      --*) ;;
      -*F*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
    esac
    case "$tok" in
      --*) ;;
      -*d*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
    esac
  done

  return 0
}

# unquoted_text_ok RAW -> 0 when the segment's shell text is plain. Outside
# quotes only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ % + , : - = and spaces are allowed, and a word
# may not start with = (zsh =cmd) or ~. That rules out braces, globs, glob
# qualifiers, expansions, backslashes, redirects and history bangs in one go.
# Single-quoted text is literal. Double-quoted text may not contain $ ` \ or !.
unquoted_text_ok() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | LC_ALL=C awk '
    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; ws = 1 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double; ws: still at word start
    { n = length($0)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        c = substr($0, i, 1)
        if (st == 1) { if (c == "\047") st = 0; else ws = 0 }
        else if (st == 2) {
          if (c == "\"") st = 0
          else {
            ws = 0
            if (c == "$" || c == "`" || c == "\\" || c == "!") bad = 1
          }
        } else if (c == " ") ws = 1
        else if (c == "\047") st = 1            # quotes alone do not end word start
        else if (c == "\"") st = 2
        else if (c == "\\") {                   # only \'"'"', \" and "\ " are literal
          nx = substr($0, i + 1, 1)
          if (nx == "\047" || nx == "\"" || nx == " ") { i++; ws = 0 } else bad = 1
        }
        else if (c ~ /[A-Za-z0-9._\/@%+,:-]/) ws = 0
        else if (c == "=" && !ws) ws = 0
        else bad = 1
      } }
    END { exit (bad || st != 0) ? 1 : 0 }'
}

# cat_ls_segment_ok MASKED -> 0 when a cat / ls segment needs no quoting,
# expansion or parent-directory access
cat_ls_segment_ok() {
  local tok p
  case "$1" in *[\"\']*|*..*) return 1 ;; esac
  has_expansion "$1" && return 1
  set -f
  set -- $1
  set +f
  case "$1" in
    ls)
      shift
      for tok in "$@"; do
        case "$tok" in
          --r*) return 1 ;;            # --recursive (and abbreviations)
          --*) ;;
          -*R*) return 1 ;;            # -R, -laR, ...
          -*) ;;
          *)  p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1   # symlink-resolved path argument
              case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac ;;
        esac
      done ;;
    cat)
      shift
      for tok in "$@"; do        # symlink-resolved: must stay in .harness/ or docs/
        p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1
        raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
        case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
      done ;;
  esac
  return 0
}

# bash_ok COMMAND -> 0 when COMMAND is one simple command on the allowlist
bash_ok() {
  local cmd=$1 out seg raw tab
  tab=$(printf '\t')
  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
  cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | tr '\t' ' ')
  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | scan_command) || return 1
  seg=${out%%"$tab"*}
  raw=${out#*"$tab"}
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
  raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
  [ -n "$seg" ] || return 1
  # plain shell text only (character allowlist)
  unquoted_text_ok "$raw" || return 1
  # reject '..' path components (but not git ranges like main...HEAD)
  printf ' %s ' "$seg" | grep -Eq '[ /=]\.\.([ /]|$)' && return 1
  case "$seg" in
    git\ *)          git_segment_ok "$raw" || return 1
                     ;;
    gh|gh\ *)        gh_segment_ok "$seg" "$raw" || return 1 ;;
    cat\ *|ls|ls\ *) cat_ls_segment_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq "$BASH_ALLOW"
}

case "$TOOL" in
  Edit|Write)
    writable "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_WRITE" ;;
  Read)
    readable "$(field file_path)" || deny "$MSG_READ" ;;
  Grep)
    readable "$(field path)" || deny "$MSG_READ"
    # a directory search would read the raw streams under .harness/log
    GRP=$(physrel "$(field path)") || deny "$MSG_READ"
    case "$GRP" in .harness|.harness/log) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac ;;

    PATTERN=$(field pattern)

  Bash)
    BCMD=$(field command)
    printf '%s' "$BCMD" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*harness[[:space:]]+["'"'"']?watch["'"'"']?([[:space:]]|$)' && deny "$MSG_WATCH"

esac
